rows.text: The reviewer criticizes repeated promotions for Super after lessons, while praising the range of languages and activities.
rows.reading: The complaint explicitly concerns promotion of Duolingo’s own paid offer. It does not isolate third-party ad inventory.

rows.text: The reviewer says Super removes ads, but criticizes animations and gamification in the remaining experience.
rows.reading: The low app rating concerns the flow and gamification. It does not establish that external ads remained after payment.

rows.text: The reviewer combines objections to ad frequency with technical problems in chess activities.
rows.reading: The app rating does not isolate the effect of advertising from technical failures.

rows.text: The reviewer describes frustration with energy limits, lesson rhythm and ads, and expresses an intention to quit.
rows.reading: Stated intention to quit is not measured churn. Several features contribute to the account.

rows.text: The reviewer describes a pop-up while using the phone, without enough context to locate the placement.
rows.reading: The account does not establish that the ad was served within Duolingo.

rows.text: The reviewer describes listening or audio failures, mentions audio in own-app ads, and reports difficulty resolving the issue.
rows.adContext: House ads in an audio complaint
rows.reading: The main concern is audio delivery and support, not a clean measurement of ad load.

rows.text: The reviewer alleges misleading third-party advertising and deceptive skip behavior.
rows.reading: This is an unverified allegation in one selected review, not an established finding about Duolingo or its advertisers.

rows.text: The reviewer rates the app highly and praises short ads compared with long, unskippable ads.
rows.reading: This illustrates why an ad-keyword match does not necessarily express negative ad sentiment.

rows.text: The reviewer objects to fewer opportunities to watch ads in exchange for energy.
rows.reading: The objection concerns reduced rewarded-ad access, rather than too many ads.

rows.text: The reviewer praises an experience without ads.
rows.reading: Actual entitlement and ad exposure are unknown. A review alone cannot establish the inventory policy.

rows.text: The reviewer combines objections to ads and a paywall. The text was in English despite an Indonesian request locale.
rows.reading: Request locale is collection provenance, not detected text language or reviewer residence.

rows.text: The reviewer rates the app highly and praises limited ads and payment offers that feel less intrusive.
rows.reading: This is a positive contextual example, not an estimate of the prevalence of that experience.

rows.text: The reviewer gives five stars and appreciates learning, while also making a brief objection to ads.
rows.reading: A high overall app rating can coexist with criticism of one feature.

rows.text: The reviewer praises learning and reports no disturbing ads.
rows.reading: The account does not measure actual ad frequency, ad type or inventory.

rows.text: The reviewer expresses a wish for access that is both free and without ads.
rows.reading: This expresses a preference. It does not establish willingness to pay or a measured behavioral response.

rows.text: The reviewer rates the app highly, criticizes ads in the free tier and recommends Super.
rows.reading: The review does not verify a payment or establish the causal effect of ads on conversion.

rows.title: Learner experience is a condition for expansion
rows.evidence: Among 2026 reviews with text ≥20 characters, 5,399/17,080 ad-keyword matches (31.6%) give 1–2 stars, versus 55,810/558,905 nonmatches (10.0%).
rows.interpretation: The association remains after restricting year and text length. It motivates risk measurement, rather than estimating retention loss caused by ads.
rows.implication: Compare against the current offer and measure learner outcomes together with total contribution.
rows.deck: Main Slide 8; full method in the appendix
rows.copy: Learner experience is a binding guardrail for the ad-yield test.
rows.footnote: Collected Google Play reviews, 2026, text ≥20 characters. 1–2 stars: 5,399/17,080 ad-keyword matches vs 55,810/558,905 nonmatches. Self-selected partial collection; keyword association, not causal ad impact.
rows.avoid: Do not claim that ads caused 31.6% churn or 3.2 times more user churn.

rows.title: An ad mention is not necessarily ad rejection
rows.evidence: In the same subset, 9,644/17,080 ad-keyword matches (56.5%) rate the app 4–5 stars. Contextual examples include praise for short ads.
rows.interpretation: A claim that users reject all ads is too broad. The app rating is not an isolated rating of ads.
rows.implication: Prioritize quality, relevance and value per opportunity. Do not classify an ad mention as a complaint.
rows.copy: Ad mentions are not uniformly negative: 56.5% of the matched group rated the app 4–5 stars.
rows.footnote: Same 2026, ≥20-character subset; 9,644 of 17,080 ad-keyword review IDs. Rating applies to the app, not isolated ad sentiment.
rows.avoid: Do not claim that 56.5% of users like ads or that advertiser demand is proven.

rows.title: Monetization friction extends beyond advertising
rows.evidence: Across all collected IDs, access/hearts/energy matches number 48,304. Of these, 25,371 (52.5%) give 1–2 stars. There are 8,538 ad/access overlaps.
rows.interpretation: Ad experience can overlap with lesson access, energy and paywalls. Overlapping lexical themes cannot be added or treated as causal effects.
rows.implication: Separate ad-experience measures from lesson access and paid-benefit delivery. This informs a small core test without validating Japan or returning-user fit.
rows.deck: Appendix; separate controls on Slides 6 and 8
rows.copy: Separate ad experience from lesson-access and paid-benefit friction.
rows.footnote: All 1,951,045 collected IDs. Multilingual lexical themes; access matches 48,304, low stars 25,371; ad/access overlap 8,538. Mentions are not validated complaints.
rows.avoid: Do not add the theme counts as distinct users or identify energy as the largest causal churn driver.

rows.title: Ad count alone does not define the experience
rows.evidence: Sixteen long, theme-enriched examples include Super promotions, audio failures, praise for short ads and objections to fewer rewarded-ad opportunities.
rows.interpretation: Some friction concerns house ads or reward access. These examples cannot estimate the prevalence of different ad types.
rows.implication: Preserve frequency, rewards and house-ad allocation controls. Specify duration, skippability and creative quality.
rows.deck: Main Slide 8 controls; illustrative examples in the appendix
rows.copy: Keep ad exposure, rewards and house-ad policy comparable; monitor creative quality and learner outcomes.
rows.footnote: Illustrative contextual reading of 16 deterministic, long-text, theme-enriched examples. No population prevalence or classifier-precision inference.
rows.avoid: Do not turn an unverified allegation into a finding of misconduct or treat all ad complaints as external-ad inventory.

rows.title: The collection does not show universal product rejection
rows.evidence: Across the full collection, 1,680,700/1,951,045 IDs (86.1%) give 4–5 stars. Mean rating is 4.44/5. Text under 20 characters accounts for 33.8%.
rows.interpretation: Voluntary app reviews do not establish retention, learning efficacy, paid value or population satisfaction.
rows.implication: Use this as context and counterevidence to a universal-rejection narrative, while investigating experience friction.
rows.copy: Most collected reviews rate the app highly; monetization friction still deserves a measured test.
rows.footnote: All collected unique review IDs, first-observed representation. 1,680,700 rated 4–5 stars; mean 4.4389/5. Not the official Play Store aggregate or a user-population survey.
rows.avoid: Do not call this 86.1% satisfaction among all users or an official Play Store score of 4.44.

rows.title: Reviews do not validate the ads-first revenue engine
rows.evidence: The data have no advertiser transactions, impressions, net CPM, fill, verified UK adult reach, experiment assignment, paid entitlement, retention or contribution.
rows.interpretation: UK fit, paid repeat, +12% global yield, subscription displacement and operating benefit remain assumptions or test questions.
rows.implication: Keep buyer value, ordinary paid repeat, total incremental contribution and learner safeguards as joint expansion gates.
rows.deck: Qualifiers on Slides 3–5 and the Slide 8 decision rule
rows.copy: Scale only after buyer value, total contribution and learner safeguards pass together.
rows.footnote: Review fields do not measure advertiser economics. Current strategy source: Deck_Content.json, ads-first-2.1-uk-sizing. No financial input is updated from these reviews.
rows.avoid: Do not use reviews to validate UK fit, brand lift, CPM, fill, repeat purchase, +12% yield or US$17.51m upside.

rows.assumption: Learner outcomes remain safe under comparable exposure
rows.reviewEvidence: Reviews flag an association, not an experimental effect.
rows.nextTest: Randomized current-offer comparison with comparable ad duration, rewards and house policy. Measure retention, lesson completion, NPS, paid conversion and total contribution.
rows.trigger: Hold or stop when predefined harm tolerances fail. Do not derive tolerances from review ratings.

rows.assumption: Advertisers obtain incremental consideration worth paying for
rows.nextTest: Agree the buyer outcome and randomized comparison before launch. Distinguish consideration from click-through rate.
rows.trigger: Do not scale when the result is inconclusive or the buyer outcome fails.

rows.assumption: Repeat buying occurs on ordinary media terms
rows.nextTest: Observe a second paid campaign for a new occasion or need, including discounts and co-funding in full costs.
rows.trigger: Hold or reprice when repeat depends on subsidy or contribution fails.

rows.assumption: UK adult inventory and net yield beat the current roadmap
rows.reviewEvidence: Not measured. Request locale is not UK residence.
rows.nextTest: Audit first-party eligibility, inventory and opportunity cost. Combine signed buyer budgets with deliverable impressions.
rows.trigger: Recompute or defer when inventory, fill, net CPM or displacement fail.

rows.assumption: Core routing delivers paid value and preserves access
rows.reviewEvidence: Contextual friction is relevant. Adult, returning-user and payment status are unverified.
rows.nextTest: Separate never-paid and formerly-paid accounts. Verify benefits and support access. Measure unseen-task gains and 90-day contribution.
rows.trigger: Fix delivery or defer the offer when benefits, learning gains or contribution fail.

rows.assumption: The collection represents all learners or countries
rows.reviewEvidence: The collection design does not identify this.
rows.nextTest: Use first-party cohorts or a sample with appropriate recruitment and denominators.
rows.trigger: Do not use request locale as geography, review dates as D30 retention or keywords as complaint rates.
